findings.where: Page heading, "Best Hostels in Canggu", at the top of the page on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The heading promises a ranked list of hostels, but the page has no hostels on it. The page is a short area guide, and the only mention of hostels is a notice at the very end saying listings are coming soon.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who arrives from a search for "best hostels Canggu" expects names they can compare. They read three paragraphs, find a coming-soon notice instead, and feel misled. That damages the site's honesty on their first visit, on a product whose own principle is "trust is the product".

findings.where: The coming-soon notice near the foot of the page (the red block), desktop and phone
findings.fault: The notice promises "direct-booking options alongside the major booking sites so you can compare and choose". Read plainly, that means comparing the hostel's own rate against the booking sites' prices and availability. The project is barred from showing those for comparison, so the page promises a feature the product cannot ship.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker will come back expecting a side-by-side price comparison that will never exist. The founder would also object: it is the comparison claim their partner terms forbid, and it is said in Manta's own voice.

findings.where: The coming-soon notice's alarm-red ground, desktop and phone
findings.fault: A neutral status message is set on a saturated warning-red panel, so "listings coming soon" reads like an error or outage. It is the loudest thing on the page and sits where the visitor's last impression forms.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a phone scrolls down, sees a red alert box and assumes something is broken or the site is not real. That is the wrong impression for a pre-launch brand trying to come across as effortless and trustworthy.

findings.where: End of the page, after the coming-soon notice, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The page dead-ends. Once the visitor learns listings are not live, there is no next step: no other destination guide to move on to, no way to hear when Canggu goes live, and nothing back to the destinations list except the small top nav. The page has no call to action at all.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning their next stop has decided Canggu interests them and has nowhere to go but away. The founder loses the one visitor a pre-launch guide page exists to keep.

findings.where: "How we rank" in the top nav and the footer; also Privacy, Terms and Report content in the footer
findings.fault: Each of these links leads back to this same page. "How we rank" is the site's credibility claim, that its ranking is merit-only and its method published, and it opens nothing. The legal links go nowhere either.
findings.who_objects: A careful traveller who taps "How we rank" to see why they should trust Manta's picks over a booking site's finds no method. A visitor checking Privacy or Terms finds none, which makes a new, unknown brand look unfinished or untrustworthy.

findings.where: "Good for" chips (twelve tags) and the guide copy above them
findings.fault: The guide says Canggu suits almost everyone: first-time surfers, remote workers, long stays, nightlife, yoga, budget, couples, solo travellers and more. It never says who Canggu does not suit (people who want quiet, swimmable beaches, or no scooter, for example). With no downside named, it reads as promotion rather than a judgement the visitor can use.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker came to judge whether Canggu suits them. A list that includes everyone answers nothing, and all-positive copy makes them doubt the guide's honesty and, through it, the rankings to come.

findings.fault: Above the fold, nothing says what MantaHostels is or why its view of Canggu is worth trusting. The visitor sees a generic destination blurb under a wordmark. What Manta does (a hostel-discovery site that ranks on merit) appears only in the notice at the bottom and a muted footer line.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor from search can't tell in five seconds whether this is a booking site, a blog or a content farm. They have no reason to come back to Manta rather than an established booking site.

findings.fault: Nothing dates the guide: no "updated" date and no year in the footer. Nobody is named behind it apart from a first-name email address.
findings.who_objects: Backpackers know beach towns change fast: hostels close and areas get built up. An undated guide from an unknown brand gives them no reason to believe it is current, or that a real person stands behind it.
